item.title: Instituto Sacatar: Sacatar Fellowship 2027 (Bahia, Brazil)
item.description:
Organisation: Instituto Sacatar

Location: Itaparica island, Bahia, Brazil. Open to all nationalities.

Award: Fully hosted residency: private bedroom with attached bathroom, three meals a day (except Saturday evenings, Sundays and Brazilian holidays), an individual studio suited to the discipline, weekly laundry, logistical support and airport transfer from Salvador. NO STIPEND, no airfare and no materials budget. USD 25 application fee. One French artist may additionally receive airfare and a stipend through Villa Fatumbi.

Duration: Approximately eight weeks; specific session dates are listed in the application.

Deadline: Closed 28 Aug 2026

Brazil's longest-running artist residency, on the island of Itaparica across the bay from Salvador, hosting six to eight artists per session for roughly eight weeks. Open to all creative disciplines and, unusually for this region, to all nationalities, which makes it one of the few genuinely international residencies in Latin America. Sacatar provides full hosting (private room, three meals daily, individual studio, laundry, local logistics and connections) but explicitly does NOT provide a stipend, airfare to Salvador, art materials or discretionary local expenses, so applicants must fund their own travel. Individual artists only; group proposals are not accepted and former Sacatar Fellows may not reapply. COVID vaccination is required. NOTE: there is a USD 25 application fee. Apply through SlideRoom by 28 August 2026. Contact info@sacatar.org.

item.title: Red Quincho: Beca Constelaciones 2026 (4th Edition)
item.description:
Organisation: Red Quincho

Location: Rotating urban and rural Red Quincho spaces across Argentina; residency runs September to December 2026.

Award: ARS 1,000,000 (around USD 690) per grant toward mobility, living costs and production, plus one month of lodging. 15 grants available. No application fee.

Duration: One-month residency split into two 15-day placements at different spaces.

Deadline: Closed 09 Aug 2026

Beca Constelaciones is Red Quincho's mobility and production grant for artists, curators and researchers doing territory-based work, now in its fourth edition. Each recipient spends one month in residence, split into two 15-day placements at different member spaces across Argentina, pairing an urban and a rural context. The grant covers mobility, living costs and production, with lodging provided. Backed by Fundacion Williams, CCEBA and Fundacion Santander through the CABA Mecenazgo scheme. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: of the 15 grants, 13 are for people resident in Argentina and 2 are for people currently living in Spain. Artists, curators and researchers apply through separate forms; Spanish-based candidates face an additional jury evaluation. Deadline 9 August 2026 at 23:59 Argentina time.
